summary: Intermittent request timeouts for EU customers caused by cross-region routing to us-east during peering flap
description: Issue summary: Since 2026-03-12 10:40 UTC we have received multiple reports from EU customers (notably Inkwell Analytics) of high tail latency and request timeouts for text-generation and streaming responses. Impact: A subset of requests from eu-west were being routed to us-east (round-trip +120ms) causing queueing in serving runtime and SDK-level timeouts for streaming sessions. Environment: prod (eu-west); affected customers primarily enterprise tier. Timeline: 10:35 - spike begins; 10:40 - first customer report; 10:52 - alerting hit p1 threshold; 11:05 - mitigation pinned region routing; 11:20 - partial recovery for pinned routes; 12:00 - continued investigation. Observed behavior: large fraction of streaming sessions fail with: SDK error: "read timeout after 120s" and gateway 504s when backend token generation exceeded 110s. Cross-region latency correlated with a peering degradation reported by cloud provider in eu-west peering fabric. This ticket captures support engagement, investigation notes, and mitigation steps.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) From an eu-west client, send a streaming chat request to /v1/chat/stream with rw-chat-3.0 and typical prompt (~800 tokens).
2) Observe SDK stream open then long silence; client eventually receives timeout at 120s or sees partial tokens then disconnect.
3) Check request routing headers X-Region-Routed-To and X-Routing-Policy in logs; observed value: us-east for affected requests.
4) Correlate with smart-router decisions in routing logs and with api-gateway connection traces to confirm cross-region proxied connections.
logs: 2026-03-12T10:42:11Z gateway[req-9a3d]: routed request region=eu-west -> target=us-east (route_policy=latency_fallback) ttl=30s
2026-03-12T10:42:13Z smart-router[decision]: evaluated peers: eu-edge-12 healthy=false last_check=00:20:07; selected us-edge-3 score=0.72
2026-03-12T10:46:37Z runtime[serve-42]: token-gen long-tail: rpc to us-east backend RTT=128ms queue-wait=88s -> 504 threshold exceeded
2026-03-12T11:02:10Z sdk-client[inkwell]: stream disconnected with error: read timeout after 120s
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: smart-router fallback to us-east due to transient eu-west peering health check failures (cloud provider reported BGP flaps).

Checked smart-router health checks: multiple eu-west edge peers marked unhealthy simultaneously; health-check interval set to 15s, but TTL for peer negative caching was 30s leading to over-eager failover.
Observed mismatch: routing rollout (PR #187) changed the fallback scoring weights last week and reduced locality bias; combination of health-check flaps and lower locality weight caused bulk reroute.
Metric correlation: spike in cross-region egress and RPC SLO violations coincident with peering event logged by provider (see provider status page).
Reproducibility: can reproduce by forcing eu-edge peers to 'unhealthy' in staging smart-router and observing routing to us-east and increased RTTs; confirms routing decision path.
customer_comments: 2026-03-12 10:50 UTC - Inkwell support: "We're seeing many streaming sessions drop and SDK timeouts, impacting customer demos. Can you confirm region is eu?"
2026-03-12 11:10 UTC - Inkwell support: "Partial recovery observed after 11:05 but still seeing increased latency for some requests. Please advise on mitigation and ETA for root cause fix."
mitigation: At 11:05 UTC ops pinned routing policy for enterprise customers in eu-west to prefer in-region endpoints and increased health-check sensitivity to avoid blackholing on brief flaps. Added temporary rate-limit exemptions for affected customer to reduce retry storms.
resolution: Temporary: pinned eu-west routes for enterprise customers and rolled back upstream routing weight change (PR #187) that reduced locality bias. Permanent: schedule change to health-check negative caching TTL and add continuous test that simulates peering flaps to validate routing behavior. Follow-up task created to harden smart-router scoring algorithm (INT-412).
resolution_notes: Customers recovered to baseline by 11:25 UTC after pinning. Post-incident, we will deploy: 1) revert routing weight change in production (done 2026-03-12 11:45 UTC), 2) lower negative-cache TTL to 5s for edge peer health, 3) add canary that simulates transient peer failure. Owner: Maya Patel / Networking team.
next_steps: Schedule code rollback verification for routing PR #187 in staging (owner: infra-team).
Create automated integration test for peering flaps in CI (owner: SRE).
Contact cloud provider to request postmortem for the eu-west peering anomaly and retain their timeline (owner: Partnerships).
Communicate summary and RCA draft to Inkwell and impacted customers (owner: CS - Nora Vega).
